content: Tolmetin sodium is available in a formulation equivalent to 200 mg of tolmetin, with tablets scored for 100 mg. Each tablet contains 784 mEq of sodium along with the following inactive ingredients: magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, pregelatinized starch, sodium starch glycolate, and talc. Tolmetin sodium is freely soluble in water. Tolmetin sodium is classified as a nonselective nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). Pharmacodynamics There is limited information available regarding the pharmacodynamics of tolmetin in the drug label. Pharmacokinetics In patients with rheumatoid arthritis and in healthy volunteers, tolmetin sodium is rapidly and almost completely absorbed, with peak plasma levels achieved within 30 to 60 minutes after an oral therapeutic dose. Controlled studies have shown that the time to reach peak plasma concentration is approximately 20 minutes longer when a 600 mg tablet is administered compared to an equivalent dose given as three 200 mg tablets. The clinical significance of this finding is unknown. Tolmetin exhibits biphasic elimination from the plasma, consisting of a rapid phase with a half-life of 1 to 2 hours, followed by a slower phase with a half-life of approximately 5 hours. Peak plasma levels of approximately 40 µg/mL are achieved with a 400 mg oral dose. Nearly all of the administered dose is recovered in the urine within 24 hours, either as an inactive oxidative metabolite or as conjugates of tolmetin. An 18-day multiple-dose study demonstrated no accumulation of tolmetin compared to a single dose. In two fecal blood loss studies lasting 4 to 6 days and involving 15 subjects each, tolmetin sodium did not cause an increase in blood loss compared to a 4-day drug-free control period. In the same studies, aspirin caused greater blood loss than observed during the drug-free control period and greater blood loss than during the tolmetin sodium treatment period. In one of the two studies, indomethacin caused greater fecal blood loss than during the drug-free control period; in the second study, indomethacin did not induce a significant increase in blood loss. Clinical Efficacy Tolmetin sodium is effective in treating both acute flares and in the long-term management of symptoms associated with rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. In patients with rheumatoid arthritis or osteoarthritis, tolmetin sodium is as effective as aspirin and indomethacin in controlling disease activity. However, the frequency of milder gastrointestinal adverse effects and tinnitus was lower in tolmetin-treated patients compared to those treated with aspirin, and the incidence of central nervous system adverse effects was lower compared to indomethacin-treated patients. In patients with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, tolmetin sodium is as effective as aspirin in controlling disease activity, with a similar incidence of adverse reactions. Mean SGOT (serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase) values, which were initially elevated in patients on prior aspirin therapy, remained elevated in the aspirin group but decreased in the tolmetin sodium group. Tolmetin sodium has shown additional therapeutic benefits when added to a regimen of gold salts and, to a lesser extent, with corticosteroids. However, tolmetin sodium should not be used in conjunction with salicylates, as the combination is unlikely to provide greater benefit and may increase the potential for adverse reactions. Nonclinical Toxicology Long-term studies have shown that tolmetin sodium does not possess carcinogenic potential. A 24-month study in rats at doses up to 75 mg/kg/day and an 18-month study in mice at doses up to 50 mg/kg/day revealed no evidence of carcinogenicity. Additionally, tolmetin sodium demonstrated no mutagenic potential in the Ames Salmonella-Microsomal Activation Test. Reproductive studies showed no impairment of fertility in animals, although effects on parturition have been observed, consistent with other prostaglandin inhibitors. This information is detailed in the Pregnancy section of the drug label. Clinical Studies There is limited information available regarding clinical studies of tolmetin in the drug label. How Supplied Tolmetin sodium is supplied as capsules and tablets: Capsules equivalent to 400 mg tolmetin, orange/orange, imprinted with Mutual. Tablets equivalent to 200 mg tolmetin, off-white, round, scored, debossed with MP 50. Storage Tolmetin sodium should be stored at 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F). Dispense in a tight, light-resistant container. Patient Counseling Information Patients should be informed of the following before initiating therapy with an NSAID and periodically during ongoing therapy. They should also be encouraged to read the NSAID Medication Guide accompanying each prescription. 1. Cardiovascular Risks: Tolmetin sodium, like other NSAIDs, may cause serious cardiovascular side effects, such as myocardial infarction (MI) or stroke, which can result in hospitalization or death. Serious cardiovascular events can occur without warning symptoms. Patients should be alert for signs and symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, or slurred speech and seek medical advice if these occur. Patients should be made aware of the importance of follow-up. 2. Gastrointestinal Risks: Tolmetin sodium, like other NSAIDs, can cause gastrointestinal discomfort and, rarely, serious gastrointestinal side effects such as ulcers and bleeding, which may result in hospitalization or death. Serious gastrointestinal tract ulcerations and bleeding can occur without warning symptoms. Patients should be alert for signs and symptoms such as epigastric pain, dyspepsia, melena, or hematemesis and seek medical advice if these occur. Patients should be made aware of the importance of follow-up. 3. Skin Reactions: Tolmetin sodium, like other NSAIDs, can cause serious skin side effects such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), which may result in hospitalization or death. Serious skin reactions may occur without warning. Patients should be alert for signs and symptoms such as skin rash, blisters, fever, or other signs of hypersensitivity, such as itching, and seek medical advice if these occur.
